fw-01.why: 안녕하세요 is used morning, noon, and night.

fw-01.q: Say thank you politely in Korean.
fw-01.why: 감사합니다 is the standard polite way to say thank you.

fw-01.hint: Watch the spelling: ㅂ, not ㅁ, in the third syllable.
fw-01.why: It is spelled 감사합니다, though pronounced [감사함니다].
커피 여기 있어요 — “Here is your coffee.”

fw-01.q: What does the customer say in reply?
fw-01.why: The customer replies with 감사합니다 (Thank you).

steps.en: Hello. Really nice to meet you.

items: I can greet anyone politely with 안녕하세요.
I can say thank you with 감사합니다.
I can apologize or say excuse me with 죄송합니다.

fw-02.why: 학생 ends in a consonant, so 이에요.

fw-02.q: Introduce yourself in one sentence: “I am ___.” (your name or job)
fw-02.why: Name ending in a vowel → 예요, in a consonant → 이에요.
한국 사람이 아니에요 — “I am not Korean.”

steps.en: I am a Korean-language student in Seoul.

items: I can say my name: “저는 ○○예요.”
I can say my job: “저는 학생이에요.”
I can choose 예요 or 이에요 by the last sound.

fw-03.why: 이거 means 'this' and 뭐예요 means 'what is it?'.

fw-03.q: Ask what something near you is: “What is this?”
fw-03.why: Point to something near you and ask 이거 뭐예요?

fw-03.hint: 뭐 ends in a vowel, so use 예요.
fw-03.why: Nouns ending in a vowel take 예요, not 에요 or 이에요.
한국어 책이에요 — “It is a Korean book.”

steps.en: This is an interesting Korean book.

items: I can distinguish 이거 (this), 그거 (that), and 저거 (that over there).
I can ask what an object is with 이거 뭐예요?
I can answer with [noun] + 예요 / 이에요.

fw-04.q: State a price ending in 원 (e.g. 5,000 won or 10,000 won).
fw-04.why: Combine Sino-Korean numbers with the currency unit 원.

fw-04.hint: Korean has a specific unit for 10,000.
fw-04.why: In Korean, 10,000 is 만, not 십천.

items: I can count from 1 to 10 in Sino-Korean numbers.
I can understand large numbers: 백 (100), 천 (1,000), 만 (10,000).
I can read and say prices in Korean Won (원).

fw-05.why: 이거 means 'this' and 얼마예요 means 'how much is it?'.

fw-05.q: Politely order an item using 주세요 (e.g. coffee or water).
fw-05.why: Put the item first, then 주세요.

fw-05.hint: 둘 changes form before a counter.
fw-05.why: Before a counter noun like 잔, 둘 becomes 두.

en: Welcome. What can I get for you?
Please give me two cups of coffee.

fw-05.q: How much is one cup of coffee?
fw-05.why: 한 잔에 삼천 원이에요 — 3,000 won per cup.

fw-05.q: How many cups did the customer order?
fw-05.why: 커피 두 잔 주세요 — two cups.

items: I can ask the price of an item with 이거 얼마예요?
I can order items using 주세요.
I can use native number counters like 한 잔 and 두 개.

fw-06.why: 화장실 means restroom and 어디예요 means where is it.

fw-06.q: Ask where a place is (e.g. the station or restroom).
fw-06.why: Put the location first, then ask 어디예요?
Nouns ending in a vowel take 예요, so it is 어디예요.

en: Yes, how can I help you?
It is over there, next to the convenience store.

fw-06.q: What place is the speaker looking for?
fw-06.why: 지하철역 어디예요? — “Where is the subway station?”
저기 편의점 옆이에요 — “Next to the convenience store over there.”

steps.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom here?

items: I can ask where places like restrooms and stations are with 어디예요?
I can point out locations with 여기 (here) and 저기 (over there).
I can call for attention in a restaurant with 여기요!

fw-07.hint: Three syllables + two syllables + two syllables.
fw-07.why: 한국어 means Korean language, 조금 means a little, 해요 means I do/speak.

fw-07.q: Tell someone that you speak a little Korean.
fw-07.why: Use 조금 (a little) to soften your statement.

fw-07.hint: Korean has a dedicated word for 'don't know'.
fw-07.why: Use 몰라요 to say 'I don't know', not 아니요 알아요.
아니요, 미국 사람이에요 — “No, I am American.”

fw-07.q: How well does the speaker speak Korean?
fw-07.why: 아니요, 조금 해요 — “No, I speak a little.”

items: I can answer simply with 네 (yes) and 아니요 (no).
I can say 'I speak a little Korean': 한국어 조금 해요.
I can admit when I don't know something: 몰라요.

fw-08.why: 이거 (this) + 두 잔 (two cups) + 주세요 (please give me).

fw-08.q: Write a complete order at a cafe or shop asking for something.
fw-08.why: Use 주세요 to politely complete your transaction.
Use native Korean numbers (두) with counter 잔, not Sino-Korean numbers (이).

en: Please give me two cups of coffee.
Yes, it is 8,000 won. Here you are.

fw-08.q: What is the total price for two cups?
fw-08.why: 네, 팔천 원이에요 — “Yes, it is 8,000 won.”

fw-08.q: What does the customer say at the end?

items: I can carry out a complete basic purchase in Korean.
I can greet, ask the price, order with quantities, and say thank you.
I can understand spoken responses like 가격 (price) and 여기 있어요 (here it is).
